description: This group mixes two plot types. The dominant panel is an Ashby-style scatter comparison of mechanical properties: x-axis "Yield strength, Rp0.2 (MPa)" (300-1000, ticks every 100); left blue y-axis "Charpy impact energy (J/cm2)" (0-200, ticks every 40); right red y-axis "Total elongation (%)" (0-100, ticks every 20). Blue filled/open up-triangles, right-triangles, squares and circles cluster at low yield strength (x between the 300 and 500 MPa gridlines) and span the full impact-energy range up to the top-left corner, while a few open blue symbols drop to near-zero energy near the 880-900 MPa gridlines. Red open triangles, filled squares and circles plot elongation of the stronger alloys (x between ~750 and 960 MPa), mostly between 0 and 45 % on the right axis; three green filled stars lie at x between ~490 and 630 MPa in the upper-middle region. No marker key is printed, so which symbol denotes HR82 cannot be read from the pixels. The second image, internally labelled "(a)", is a dual-axis line plot: x-axis "Hot-rolling reduction (%)" (40-85), left y-axis "Mean grain size (µm)" (0-70), right y-axis "Dislocation density (×10^13 m^-2)" (0-14); legend black open squares "Grain size (excluding twins)", blue open circles "Effective grain size (including twins)", red open triangles "Dislocation density". With increasing reduction the two grain-size curves fall and the dislocation-density curve rises, all with error bars that are largest at the lowest reduction.

observations.observation: The scatter panel has no legend or marker key, so no symbol can be assigned to a named alloy from the pixels alone.
Blue markers (Charpy impact energy, left axis) cluster between the 300 and 500 MPa gridlines and include the highest points in the plot, in the top-left region.
Several open blue symbols lie close to the 880-900 MPa gridlines with impact-energy values at or just above the zero line.
Red markers, read against the right-hand Total elongation (%) axis, scatter between roughly the 750 and 960 MPa gridlines and mostly stay below the 45 % level.
Three green filled stars appear at x between about 490 and 630 MPa and in the upper-middle of the impact-energy field.

In the second image the black curve ('Grain size (excluding twins)') starts near the 46 µm level at the lowest reduction point and descends to just below the 20 µm gridline at the highest reduction point.
In the second image the blue curve ('Effective grain size (including twins)') lies below the black curve throughout and falls from about the 22 µm level to roughly the 7 µm level.
In the second image the red curve ('Dislocation density') rises monotonically from about 2.5 to about 9.5 ×10^13 m^-2 as hot-rolling reduction increases from the lowest to the highest data point.
In the second image error bars are plotted on all three series and are visibly largest at the lowest hot-rolling reduction.

The caption states the figure compares mechanical properties of the HR82 sample with SUS347J1TB austenitic stainless steels (ASS) [29], nickel-free ASS [26], super ASS [30], and other Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steels [26-28, 31-36].
The caption does not mention grain size or dislocation density, so the second image (internally labelled '(a)') is not described by the supplied Fig. 7 caption.

The citing text states HR82 reached a similar ductility (~50%) and toughness (~100 J/m^2) to solution-treated austenitic stainless steels and Fe-Mn-Al-C alloys while its yield strength was markedly higher.

The citing text states the HR82 yield strength is comparable to an aging-hardened austenitic low-density steel (~650 MPa) but with considerably better ductility (50% vs. 21%) and toughness (105 J vs. 35 J).
The citing text gives toughness in J/m^2 (~100 J/m^2, 105 J) whereas the plotted axis is labelled J/cm^2 — a unit inconsistency between text and figure that the image cannot resolve.
The citing text attributes the property combination to increasing the hot-rolling reduction from 45% to 82%.

subfigures.description: Scatter comparison plot of Yield strength Rp0.2 (MPa) vs Charpy impact energy (J/cm2) on the blue left axis and Total elongation (%) on the red right axis. Blue symbols (filled/open triangles, squares, circles) occupy the energy field; red symbols (open triangles, filled squares, filled circles, small open squares) occupy the elongation field at higher yield strength; three green filled stars sit mid-plot. No legend or marker key is visible, so the symbol-to-study assignment is not readable.

Dual-axis line plot of hot-rolling reduction (%) versus mean grain size (µm, left axis) and dislocation density (×10^13 m^-2, right axis). Three series with error bars and a legend: black open squares 'Grain size (excluding twins)', blue open circles 'Effective grain size (including twins)', red open triangles 'Dislocation density'. Data points fall near 45%, ~68% and ~82% reduction.
